<content>
1: # Symbiosis
2: 
3: A fork of the [Eden](https://git.eden-emu.dev/eden-emu/eden) Android emulator, tuned for
4: **ARM Mali GPUs on 8 GB devices where no custom Vulkan driver can be installed**.
5: 
6: Target hardware for this work: **Mali-G57 MC2 / MediaTek MT6789, 8 GB RAM (~5 GB usable)**.
7: 
8: ---
9: 
10: ## Why this fork exists
11: 
12: Stock Eden assumes a desktop-class GPU or an Adreno with replaceable drivers. On Mali:
13: 
14: - **OpenGL is unavailable.** Eden's GL renderer requires desktop OpenGL 4.6
15:   (`gl_device.cpp:163` throws otherwise); Android offers GLES 3.2. Vulkan is the only path.
16: - **No custom drivers.** Unlike Adreno, there is no widely deployed Turnip/adrenotools
17:   equivalent. The vendor blob is all there is.
18: - **Eden has no Mali knowledge.** `vulkan_device.cpp` carries a large Qualcomm quirk block;
19:   for ARM there is nothing, even though a Bifrost G71 and an Immortalis G720 differ enormously.
20: 
21: ## Settings are requests, not guarantees
22: 
23: The core insight behind this fork. Between a toggle and the GPU sit silent filters that
24: never report back, so a setting can stay on while doing nothing:
25: 
26: | Setting | Gate | Effect on Mali |
27: |---|---|---|
28: | `astc_recompression` | `!device.IsOptimalAstcSupported()` — `maxwell_to_vk.cpp:248` | **Dead.** Mali decodes ASTC in hardware, so the value is read and discarded. |
29: | `force_max_clock` | `ShouldBoostClocks()` — `vulkan_device.cpp:947` | **Dead.** The allow-list names AMD, NVIDIA, Intel, Qualcomm, Samsung. ARM is absent. |
30: | `use_vsync` | `ChooseSwapPresentMode()` — `vk_swapchain.cpp:44` | **Renegotiated silently** against surface capabilities; caps the frame rate. |
31: | `use_asynchronous_shaders` | `vk_pipeline_cache.cpp:353` | Survives, but worker count collapses to 1 on fragile drivers. |
32: 
33: The **launch report** (Diagnostics → Launch report, or the overlay button next to the FPS
34: counter) states, per setting, whether it reached the renderer, what it became if not, and
35: which line of code decided that.
36: 
37: ---
38: 
39: ## Repository layout
40: 
41: ```
42: patch/
43:   symbiosis/              C++ layer, ~6500 lines (src/common/symbiosis/)
44:   shaders/                present_retro.frag
45:   android/                Kotlin fragments, adapters, utils, layouts, strings
46:   native_symbiosis.cpp    JNI bridge, 53 entry points
47:   upstream_changes.patch  git diff against upstream Eden
48: tools/
49:   apply_patch.sh          restores the tree into a fresh Eden checkout
50:   setup_env.sh            JDK 17 + Android SDK/NDK + swap
51:   run_build.sh            gradle assembleLegacyDebug
52: tests/
53:   t_*.cpp                 host tests for the C++ layer
54:   SetupPageTest.kt        setup-page visibility logic
55:   test_l10n.py            Russian localisation checks
56: docs/
57:   BUGS.md                 every bug found, with evidence
58: ```
59: 
60: ## Building
61: 
62: **Builds run in GitHub Actions, not on a workstation.** Go to the
63: [Actions tab](https://github.com/sj0404-collab/symbiosis/actions), pick
64: **Build APK**, press *Run workflow*. About 25 minutes; the APK is attached as an
65: artefact and, if the box is ticked, uploaded to gofile.io with its MD5 printed
66: in the run summary.
67: 
68: Three workflows:
69: 
70: | Workflow | Runs | Purpose |
71: |---|---|---|
72: | **Tests** | ~4 min | Host test suite, the localisation check and the agent/chat suite. Runs on every change to `tests/`, `tools/run_tests.sh`, the C++ layer or `agent/`. |
73: | **Build APK** | ~25 min | The above, then the full NDK build, then verifies the fixes are present in the produced APK. |
74: | **Panel APK** | ~5 min | The Symbiosis panel as a standalone, self-contained app. Independent of the emulator. |
75: 
76: ### Panel APK
77: 
78: The panel is a separate, much smaller app: the control panel for this account
79: and for the fork, with no emulator in it. **The pages are packaged inside the
80: APK**, so it opens with no connection; the network is used only for what the
81: panel actually does - the GitHub API, starting workflows, reaching a session
82: tunnel.
83: 
84: It is served to the WebView from `assets/panel/` under a private https origin
85: rather than `file://`, because the page keeps its token in `localStorage` and
86: calls `api.github.com`: a `file://` document gets an opaque origin, loses that
87: storage between launches and has its cross-origin requests blocked.
88: 
89: Because the pages ship in the APK, editing `docs/` no longer updates an
90: installed app on its own - rebuild and reinstall. The build verifies that each
91: page is really inside the APK and byte-identical to `docs/`, so a build that
92: quietly shipped an empty `assets/` fails instead of reaching a phone.
93: 
94: `ubuntu-latest` deliberately: Eden's native build is CMake + NDK and targets
95: Linux, and `windows-latest` would add path-length and line-ending failures for
96: no benefit.
97: 
98: Building locally is possible but not recommended — it needs ~6 GB of swap,
99: `kotlin.compiler.execution.strategy=in-process` to survive the OOM killer, and
100: takes over half an hour on a small machine:
101: 
102: ```bash
103: bash tools/setup_env.sh
104: git clone --depth 50 https://git.eden-emu.dev/eden-emu/eden.git /work/eden
105: bash tools/apply_patch.sh --patch ./patch --eden /work/eden
106: bash tools/run_build.sh
107: ```
108: 
109: ## Running the tests
110: 
111: ```bash
112: git clone --depth 50 https://git.eden-emu.dev/eden-emu/eden.git /tmp/eden
113: bash tools/apply_patch.sh --patch ./patch --eden /tmp/eden
114: bash tools/run_tests.sh --eden /tmp/eden
115: ```
116: 
117: Two traps the harness now guards against, both of which once made the suite
118: look green while checking nothing:
119: 
120: - **Never** put `<eden>/src/common` on the include path. Eden ships its own
121:   `common/assert.h`, which shadows the standard `<cassert>`; every `assert()`
122:   then expands to nothing.
123: - Eden's `logging.h` calls `format.get()`, which needs **fmt 10**. Ubuntu
124:   packages fmt 9, so set `FMT_INCLUDE` to a fmt 10 checkout — otherwise every
125:   test that touches the layer fails to compile and is skipped.
126: 
127: 11 of 14 tests build and run; the 3 that need most of `video_core` are reported
128: as SKIP, and the harness fails if that number grows.
129: 
130: ## Honest status
131: 
132: Everything here is verified on the host — unit tests, `llvm-nm` symbol checks,
133: `aapt2` resource dumps, and a clean re-apply of the patch onto a fresh clone.
134: **None of it has been tested on physical Android hardware**, because none is available
135: in the build environment. Where a conclusion is a guess, it is labelled as one.
136: 
137: ## Licence
138: 
139: GPL-3.0-or-later, matching upstream Eden.

(End of file - total 139 lines)
</content>

The core insight behind this fork. Between a toggle and the GPU sit silent filters that
never report back, so a setting can stay on while doing nothing:

| Setting | Gate | Effect on Mali |
|---|---|---|
| `astc_recompression` | `!device.IsOptimalAstcSupported()` — `maxwell_to_vk.cpp:248` | **Dead.** Mali decodes ASTC in hardware, so the value is read and discarded. |
| `force_max_clock` | `ShouldBoostClocks()` — `vulkan_device.cpp:947` | **Dead.** The allow-list names AMD, NVIDIA, Intel, Qualcomm, Samsung. ARM is absent. |
| `use_vsync` | `ChooseSwapPresentMode()` — `vk_swapchain.cpp:44` | **Renegotiated silently** against surface capabilities; caps the frame rate. |
| `use_asynchronous_shaders` | `vk_pipeline_cache.cpp:353` | Survives, but worker count collapses to 1 on fragile drivers. |

The **launch report** (Diagnostics → Launch report, or the overlay button next to the FPS
counter) states, per setting, whether it reached the renderer, what it became if not, and
which line of code decided that.

---

## Repository layout

```
patch/
  symbiosis/              C++ layer, ~6500 lines (src/common/symbiosis/)
  shaders/                present_retro.frag
  android/                Kotlin fragments, adapters, utils, layouts, strings
  native_symbiosis.cpp    JNI bridge, 53 entry points
  upstream_changes.patch  git diff against upstream Eden
tools/
  apply_patch.sh          restores the tree into a fresh Eden checkout
  setup_env.sh            JDK 17 + Android SDK/NDK + swap
  run_build.sh            gradle assembleLegacyDebug
tests/
  t_*.cpp                 host tests for the C++ layer
  SetupPageTest.kt        setup-page visibility logic
  test_l10n.py            Russian localisation checks
docs/
  BUGS.md                 every bug found, with evidence
```

## Building

**Builds run in GitHub Actions, not on a workstation.** Go to the
[Actions tab](https://github.com/sj0404-collab/symbiosis/actions), pick
**Build APK**, press *Run workflow*. About 25 minutes; the APK is attached as an
artefact and, if the box is ticked, uploaded to gofile.io with its MD5 printed
in the run summary.

Three workflows:

| Workflow | Runs | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| **Tests** | ~4 min | Host test suite, the localisation check and the agent/chat suite. Runs on every change to `tests/`, `tools/run_tests.sh`, the C++ layer or `agent/`. |
| **Build APK** | ~25 min | The above, then the full NDK build, then verifies the fixes are present in the produced APK. |
| **Panel APK** | ~5 min | The Symbiosis panel as a standalone, self-contained app. Independent of the emulator. |

### Panel APK

The panel is a separate, much smaller app: the control panel for this account
and for the fork, with no emulator in it. **The pages are packaged inside the
APK**, so it opens with no connection; the network is used only for what the
panel actually does - the GitHub API, starting workflows, reaching a session
tunnel.

It is served to the WebView from `assets/panel/` under a private https origin
rather than `file://`, because the page keeps its token in `localStorage` and
calls `api.github.com`: a `file://` document gets an opaque origin, loses that
storage between launches and has its cross-origin requests blocked.

Because the pages ship in the APK, editing `docs/` no longer updates an
installed app on its own - rebuild and reinstall. The build verifies that each
page is really inside the APK and byte-identical to `docs/`, so a build that
quietly shipped an empty `assets/` fails instead of reaching a phone.

`ubuntu-latest` deliberately: Eden's native build is CMake + NDK and targets
Linux, and `windows-latest` would add path-length and line-ending failures for
no benefit.

Building locally is possible but not recommended — it needs ~6 GB of swap,
`kotlin.compiler.execution.strategy=in-process` to survive the OOM killer, and
takes over half an hour on a small machine:

```bash
bash tools/setup_env.sh
git clone --depth 50 https://git.eden-emu.dev/eden-emu/eden.git /work/eden
bash tools/apply_patch.sh --patch ./patch --eden /work/eden
bash tools/run_build.sh
```

## Running the tests

```bash
git clone --depth 50 https://git.eden-emu.dev/eden-emu/eden.git /tmp/eden
bash tools/apply_patch.sh --patch ./patch --eden /tmp/eden
bash tools/run_tests.sh --eden /tmp/eden
```

Two traps the harness now guards against, both of which once made the suite
look green while checking nothing:

- **Never** put `<eden>/src/common` on the include path. Eden ships its own
  `common/assert.h`, which shadows the standard `<cassert>`; every `assert()`
  then expands to nothing.
- Eden's `logging.h` calls `format.get()`, which needs **fmt 10**. Ubuntu
  packages fmt 9, so set `FMT_INCLUDE` to a fmt 10 checkout — otherwise every
  test that touches the layer fails to compile and is skipped.

11 of 14 tests build and run; the 3 that need most of `video_core` are reported
as SKIP, and the harness fails if that number grows.

## Honest status

Everything here is verified on the host — unit tests, `llvm-nm` symbol checks,
`aapt2` resource dumps, and a clean re-apply of the patch onto a fresh clone.
**None of it has been tested on physical Android hardware**, because none is available
in the build environment. Where a conclusion is a guess, it is labelled as one.

## Licence

GPL-3.0-or-later, matching upstream Eden.

Gesture / horizontal-navigation handlers ### 5.1 WebView rail — no custom code at all - CSS: `docs/library.html:220-241` — `overflow-x:auto; overflow-y:hidden` (`:223`), `scroll-snap-type:x mandatory` (`:224`), `-webkit-overflow-scrolling:touch` (`:225`), `padding:8px 18vw` (`:226`), `scrollbar-width:none` (`:227`), `.slide { scroll-snap-align:center }` (`:232`) - Buttons: `:402` `id="ln-prev"`, `:404` `id="ln-next"` → `:1507-1508` `snapTo(LAUNCH_I ∓ 1)` - `snapTo(i)` `:808-818` — wraps index, toggles `.on`, `scrollIntoView({inline:'center', behavior:'smooth'})` - `nearestSlide()` `:820-835` — nearest by `offsetLeft + offsetWidth/2` - Driver: `:1482-1489` debounced (80 ms) **passive** `scroll` listener → `nearestSlide()` - Click: `:782-788` — clicking a non-selected slide snaps to it; clicking the selected one launches - Rotation: `:1491-1505` `keepLaunchFrame()` on `resize`/`orientationchange` - **`preventDefault` appears only at `:590` (`contextmenu`) and `:594` (long-press `touchend`) — both inside `render()`, i.e. on the Список rows, never on the rail.** There is no `touchmove`, no `pointerdown`, no `gesturestart`, no `keydown`/arrow-key handler anywhere in the file. ### 5.2 Native carousel — driven but not implemented here `patch/android/ui/GamesFragment.kt` only *drives* the upstream class: - `:146-157` view-type keys (`CAROUSEL_VIEW_TYPE_LANDSCAPE/PORTRAIT`) - `:250` `pendingScrollAfterReload = true` - `:358-362` `notifyLaidOut()` / `setupCarousel(false)`; `:359` inset handoff - `:378-379` save `lastScrollPosition` from `getClosestChildPosition()` - `:394-396` `setupCarousel(true)` + `restoreScrollState()` - `:785` `smoothScrollToPosition(0)` - `:894` `notifyInsetsReady()` - Layout: `patch/android/layout-land/fragment_games.xml:336` (`CarouselRecyclerView`); portrait is a plain `RecyclerView` inside `SwipeRefreshLayout` (`patch/android/layout/fragment_games.xml:318-359`) ## 6. "Only one game" risks — ranked **R1. Keys gate wipes the in-memory list — CONFIRMED, highest impact.** `patch/android/utils/GameHelper.kt:83-88`: if `areKeysPresent()` is false, `cachedGameList = mutableListOf()` and `emptyList()` is returned. Compounded by `LivePanel.kt:86`, which returns `emptyList()` to the WebView whenever keys are absent. The persisted `KEY_GAMES` cache survives (it is written at `:138-141`, after the early return), so the *startup* list and the *post-rescan* list can disagree. **R2. Startup is cache-only and never refreshes — CONFIRMED.** `patch/android/model/GamesViewModel.kt:55-78` `init` calls only `loadCachedGames()` (`:90-107`); `reloadGames()` is not called at init (the comment at `:61-76` explains this was deliberate, to stop the restart crash). Consequence: if the last successful scan found one game, one game is shown indefinitely until pull-to-refresh (`:195-201`) or the panel's `findGames()` (`library.html:709-727`). **R3. An empty scan result never clears the native list — CONFIRMED bug.** `patch/android/ui/GamesFragment.kt:229-233`: ``` gamesViewModel.games.collect(viewLifecycleOwner) { if (it.isNotEmpty()) { setAdapter(it) } } ``` An empty emission (R1, permission loss, or a removed folder) leaves the previous adapter list on screen, while `:224-227` makes `noticeText` visible — the "no games" notice renders over a stale list. This is exactly the "it knows the files are there but shows one/zero" family of reports. **R4. Rail built from the filtered list — HISTORICAL, verified fixed.** `docs/BUGS.md:226-285` documents the exact user report («одну игру видит… лаунчер не прокручивается влево вправо»). Cause: `renderLauncher()` used `visibleGames()`. Current `railGames()` (`:512-514`) uses the full library, and `tests/LauncherRailTest.kt` asserts the shipped HTML — including that `docs/` and `patch/android/assets/` copies are byte-identical. **The remaining part of that report is still true as presentation:** `padding:8px 18vw` + `min(42vw,220px)` slides + hidden scrollbar (`BUGS.md:252-256`) means a full library still *looks* like one tile. **R5. Depth cap hides one-folder-per-game libraries — CONFIRMED by design.** `GameHelper.kt:110` uses depth 1 when `deepScan` is off. A library organised as `Games/GameName/game.nsp` yields **0** games. Pinned as intended by `tests/GameCountTest.kt` ("depth 1 misses a nested game, as upstream does"). **R6. Hard caps — CONFIRMED.** `MAX_DIRECTORIES = 400` (`GameFolderScanner.kt:505`, used at `:257`, `:368`, `:484`) and `MAX_ENTRIES = 3000` (`:514`, used at `:73`, `:378`, `:396`). A tree wider/deeper than 400 directories is silently truncated — count and list truncate together, so no drift, but games are missed with no "truncated" indication. Also `LivePanel.kt:377` (`steps < 80`) and `:391` (`steps < 40`) cap save/mode byte walks. **R7. Per-folder counts use path-prefix matching that can silently fail — RISK.** `LivePanel.kt:58-61` matches cached `Game.path` against `GameFolderScanner.pathOf(dir.uriString)`. `pathOf` (`:177-182`) normalizes SAF URIs by taking the text after the last `:`; a plain `/storage/emulated/0/...` path has no `:` prefix handling difference, but a URI whose percent-encoding differs from the stored `Game.path` yields no prefix match → folder reads "0 игр" while the library has games. This is the only place where a folder can claim zero while the rail is non-empty. **R8. `rememberedGames()` never scans — CONFIRMED design.** `LivePanel.kt:85-106`. The panel list is a pure mirror of the last native scan; the only trigger is `Symbiosis.rescan()` → `LivePanelFragment.kt:438-442` → `gamesViewModel.reloadGames(false)`. **R9. `patch2` uses stricter format policy — DIVERGENCE (not a bug; the overlays are not combined).** `patch2/android/utils/GameFolderScanner.kt:30` accepts only `{xci, nsp, nca, nro}`; `patch2/android/utils/GameHelper.kt:209` uses upstream `Game.extensions` only. `patch2/tests/MyGamesTest.kt` mirrors that narrower set. Applying `patch2` would drop `nso`, `kip`, and files named `main`/`00` that `patch/` keeps. **R10. `Bridge.rescan()` does not notify the page — CONFIRMED, cosmetic.** `LivePanelFragment.kt:438-442` starts the scan but never calls back into JS. `findGames()` compensates by polling `loadGames()` every 700 ms for up to 20 iterations (`library.html:717-726`). Any other `rescan()` caller gets a silent update. **No confirmed occurrence** of `first()`/`firstOrNull()` truncation, a one-element adapter, or an early `break` in any game-list path. ## 7. Horizontal-navigation risks **H1. The rail has zero custom gesture handling — everything depends on the browser.** `library.html:223-232` only. If the WebView is not Chromium (or scroll-snap is disabled by a plugin), the rail degrades to a plain scroller with no snap and no keyboard support (there is no `keydown`/arrow handling anywhere). **H2. No drag suppression on the cover images — most likely real-world failure.** `.slide img` (`:242`) sets only `width/height/object-fit/display`. There is **no `user-select:none`, no `-webkit-user-drag:none`, no `draggable="false"`, no `-webkit-touch-callout:none`** anywhere in the file (grep for `draggable|user-select|-webkit-touch-callout` returns zero hits). The covers are `data:image/jpeg;base64` `` injected by `fillCover()` (`:800-806`). A long press on a cover is a native image-drag gesture on many Android WebViews, which pre-empts the horizontal swipe. **H3. `scrollIntoView` is the only positioning mechanism** (`:796`, `:816`, `:1393`, `:1495`). `scrollIntoView` scrolls **all scrollable ancestors**; with `block:'nearest'` it normally leaves the page alone, but it is the classic way a rail steals vertical scroll. There is no `rail.scrollTo({left: …})` fallback. **H4. `renderLauncher()` rebuilds the rail wholesale and re-centers — drops the user's place mid-gesture.** Called from three places: `loadGames()` (`:1076`, and `loadGames` runs from `findGames` polling at `:720`, from `onFolderAdded` at `:1129`, from `onSavesPicked` at `:1135`, from folder removal at `:1106`), `showTab('launch')` (`:1390`), and the tools sort/filter bar (`:1476`). Each call replaces `rail.innerHTML` (`:778`) and re-issues `scrollIntoView` in `requestAnimationFrame` (`:794-797`). A 700 ms rescan poll landing mid-swipe resets the rail to `LAUNCH_I`. **H5. `nearestSlide()` measures untransformed boxes while the slides are visually scaled.** `:826` uses `offsetLeft + offsetWidth/2`; `.slide` is `transform:scale(.88)` (`:238`) expanding to `scale(1)` when `.on` (`:241`). The centers are geometrically correct, but the highlighted tile and the tile the user perceives as centred can differ by the transform, and the `transform` is animating over 0.18 s (`:239`) while the 80 ms scroll debounce (`:1487`) fires — so `.on` can land on the previous tile during a fast flick. **H6. Landscape relayout.** `:344-359` switches slides to `min(28vh,180px)` and `padding:6px 44px`, and the rail-wrap to `flex:0 0 36%; max-width:320px` (`:351`). `keepLaunchFrame()` (`:1491-1505`) re-centers on `resize` and twice on `orientationchange`. Combined with `snapTo`'s `scrollIntoView`, a rotation during a fling can leave the rail between two snap points with `.on` set on one of them. **H7. In Kenji space there is no horizontal navigation at all.** `:341` `body.space-kenji #view-launch, #view-games { display:none !important; }` and `:342` hides the tabs; `paintSpaces()` (`:1531-1536`) shows `#view-kenji` with the vertical `#k-grid` (`:1562-1595`). `renderKenjiGrid` has its **own** search box (`:1565-1566`, wired at `:1626`) independent of `visibleGames()` — a second filter surface that can disagree with the Список tab. The «Их APK» button in that bar (`:1629-1632`) acts on `RAIL_LIST[LAUNCH_I]`, i.e. on the **hidden** rail's selection, which is not what the Kenji grid highlights — a genuine cross-surface mismatch. **H8. Portrait native screen has no horizontal pager.** `patch/android/layout/fragment_games.xml:318-359` is `SwipeRefreshLayout` → plain `RecyclerView`. The native carousel exists only in `layout-land/fragment_games.xml:336`. So the only place where a *parent view* could steal a horizontal gesture on the native side is `SwipeRefreshLayout` — I cannot verify its interception rules without the upstream `CarouselRecyclerView`/`SwipeRefreshLayout` sources. **H9. ViewHolder reuse across view types is guarded, but carousel restore is best-effort.** `GamesFragment.kt:328-330` forces a non-carousel view type on holders left over from the carousel, and `:356-362` re-runs `notifyLaidOut`/`setupCarousel`. `lastScrollPosition` (`:53` in the ViewModel) is a single `Int` shared by all view types, so switching grid→carousel→list→carousel restores a position computed for a different layout manager. ## 8. Test coverage Runner: `tools/run_tests.sh` (C++ against a patched Eden tree, then all `tests/*.kt` via `kotlinc`, then all `tests/*.js` via node). **Not run here** — it needs `EDEN_DIR` (default `/tmp/citest`) which does not exist, it creates a build dir via `mktemp -d` (→ `/tmp`, contrary to `MANIFEST.md:11-14`), and the task forbids creating files. | Test | Covers | |---|---| | `tests/LauncherRailTest.kt:24-170` | The one-game bug. Mirrors `sortGames`/`visibleGames`/`railGames`, then asserts against the **shipped HTML**: `railGames()` exists, `RAIL_LIST = railGames()` and **not** `visibleGames()`, no `$('q')`/`FILTER ===` inside `railGames`, `GAMES.slice()` present, `visibleGames` is the only search site, the `N / M` counter exists (`:146-153`), both HTML copies byte-identical (`:126-129`) | | `tests/GameFormatsTest.kt:9-44` | `LAUNCHABLE`/`NAMES`/`COMPRESSED` vs `loader.cpp` | | `tests/GameCountTest.kt:20-77` | NSO/KIP accepted; depth 1 vs 3; depth-3 ceiling; byte summing | | `tests/FolderScanTest.kt:20-186` | Counter/lister parity, `relativePath`, largest-first ordering, empty folder, 500-deep tree vs the 400 guard, byte summing | | `tests/LazyScanTest.kt:18-197` | No invented folder, parent-of-child collapse, layout names never descended, status line reads cache | | `tests/GameFormatsTest`/`tests/SetupPageTest.kt` | Wizard and status wording | | `tests/LauncherUiTest.kt:21-94` | Card filters/sorts, `wrapIndex` wrap-around, CPU cycling, engine selection | | `tests/PanelAssetsTest.kt` | Panel routing, traversal refusal, `docs/` pages present, shell has no github.io URL | | `tests/SpacesTest.kt:7-31` | Workspace normalisation | | `patch2/tests/{FolderScan,GroupByFolder,CardSubtitle,MyGames,StatusVerdict,GameFolders}Test.kt` | Alternate-overlay models | **Coverage gaps relevant to this audit:** no test asserts anything about `.rail` CSS (overflow-x, scroll-snap, padding), the `‹ ›` buttons, `snapTo` wrap-around against the real DOM, image drag suppression, or `renderLauncher()` re-entrancy. `LauncherRailTest` proves the *data* is right; nothing proves the *gesture* works. `tests/t_*.cpp/js` are C++/agent tests and touch none of this. ## 9. Blocked `CarouselRecyclerView` and `GameAdapter` are not in the repository. Their touch handling (`onInterceptTouchEvent`, `onTouchEvent`, fling/snap), the `notifyLaidOut`/`setupCarousel`/`getClosestChildPosition` implementations, and `card_game_carousel.xml`'s inflation cannot be inspected here — only their call sites. Everything else above is verified against source in this repo.

202:                 if (a.isEmpty()) continue
203:                 if (b.startsWith("$a/")) keep[i] = false
204:                 if (a == b && j < i) keep[i] = false
205:             }
206:         }
207:         return uris.filterIndexed { i, _ -> keep[i] }
208:     }
209: 
210:     /** Scan one folder, for callers that have a uri rather than the config. */
211:     fun scanOneFolder(
212:         context: Context,
213:         uriString: String,
214:         deepScan: Boolean,
215:         stillWanted: () -> Boolean = { true }
216:     ): Folder = scanOne(context, uriString, depthFor(deepScan), stillWanted)
217: 
218:     /**
219:      * @param stillWanted спрашивается перед каждым каталогом. Отмена
220:      *   корутины НЕ прерывает обычный цикл и не выставляет флаг
221:      *   прерывания потока - Dispatchers.IO просто отпускает результат, а
222:      *   код продолжает читать диск. Поэтому признак передаётся явно.
223:      */
224:     private fun scanOne(
225:         context: Context,
226:         uriString: String,
227:         maxDepth: Int,
228:         stillWanted: () -> Boolean = { true }
229:     ): Folder {
230:         // Контекст приложения, а не тот, что передали.
231:         //
232:         // Обход папки живёт секунды, а вызывают его из фрагмента, который
233:         // за это время может закрыться - поворот экрана, уход в
234:         // «Настройки» за разрешением. Курсор ContentResolver держит
235:         // ссылку на контекст: если это контекст фрагмента, вся активность
236:         // вместе с макетами остаётся в памяти до конца обхода. У этого
237:         // экрана обход запускается при каждом onResume, и каждый поворот
238:         // добавлял ещё одну утёкшую активность.
239:         val resolver = context.applicationContext.contentResolver
240:         val name = displayNameOf(uriString)
241:         val tree = runCatching { Uri.parse(uriString) }.getOrNull()
242:             ?: return Folder(uriString, name, 0, 0, depth = maxDepth, unreadable = true)
243: 
244:         var count = 0
245:         var bytes = 0L
246:         var skipped = 0
247:         var readable = false
248: 
249:         // Iterative rather than recursive: a pathological tree should not be
250:         // able to overflow the stack on a screen this trivial.
251:         val queue = ArrayDeque<Pair<Uri, Int>>()
252:         queue.add((childrenUriFor(tree)
253:             ?: return Folder(uriString, name, 0, 0, depth = maxDepth, unreadable = true)) to maxDepth)
254: 
255:         var guard = 0
256:         val seen = HashSet<String>()
257:         while (queue.isNotEmpty() && guard < MAX_DIRECTORIES) {
258:             guard++
259:             // Прервать обход, когда результат уже никому не нужен.
260:             //
261:             // Экран закрыли или запросили новый обход: до 400 запросов к
262:             // хранилищу, каждый со своим курсором, продолжались бы
263:             // впустую. Пользователь ушёл, а телефон ещё несколько секунд
264:             // читает диск.
265:             if (!stillWanted()) break
266:             val (children, depth) = queue.removeFirst()
267:             val cursor = runCatching {
268:                 resolver.query(
269:                     children,
270:                     arrayOf(
271:                         DocumentsContract.Document.COLUMN_DOCUMENT_ID,
272:                         DocumentsContract.Document.COLUMN_DISPLAY_NAME,
273:                         DocumentsContract.Document.COLUMN_MIME_TYPE,
274:                         DocumentsContract.Document.COLUMN_SIZE
275:                     ),
276:                     null, null, null
277:                 )
278:             }.getOrNull() ?: continue
279: 
280:             readable = true
281:             // cursor.use закрывает курсор при выходе, НО не при исключении
282:             // внутри самого перебора: getString на битой строке кидает, и
283:             // раньше это исключение уходило наверх, обрывая весь обход.
284:             // Одна нечитаемая запись делала папку целиком "пустой".
285:             runCatching {
286:             cursor.use {
287:                 while (it.moveToNext()) {
288:                     val documentId = it.getString(0)
289:                     val displayName = it.getString(1) ?: ""
290:                     val mimeType = it.getString(2) ?: ""
291:                     val size = if (it.isNull(3)) 0L else it.getLong(3)
292: 
293:                     if (mimeType == DocumentsContract.Document.MIME_TYPE_DIR) {
294:                         // Пускать в очередь только новые каталоги.
295:                         //
296:                         // Провайдер вполне может вернуть один и тот же
297:                         // documentId дважды: сетевые и облачные хранилища
298:                         // делают это на папках, доступных по нескольким
299:                         // путям. Раньше такая пара каталогов гоняла обход
300:                         // по кругу, пока не упрётся в лимит 400 - и
301:                         // считала одни и те же файлы много раз.
302:                         if (depth > 1 && documentId != null && seen.add(documentId)) {
303:                             runCatching {
304:                                 queue.add(
305:                                     DocumentsContract.buildChildDocumentsUriUsingTree(
306:                                         tree, documentId
307:                                     ) to depth - 1
308:                                 )
309:                             }
310:                         }
311:                         continue
312:                     }
313: 
314:                     val ext = displayName.substringAfterLast('.', "").lowercase(Locale.ROOT)
315:                     if (isRom(displayName)) {
316:                         count++
317:                         bytes += size
318:                     } else if (ext in NON_GAME_EXTENSIONS) {
319:                         skipped++
320:                     }
321:                 }
322:             }
323:             }
324:         }
325: 
326:         return Folder(uriString, name, count, bytes, skipped, maxDepth, unreadable = !readable)
327:     }
328: 
329:     data class Entry(
330:         val name: String,
331:         val bytes: Long,
332:         /** Sub-path below the folder root, empty when the file sits at the top. */
333:         val relativePath: String = ""
334:     )
335: 
336:     /**
337:      * Lists the ROMs inside one folder.
338:      *
339:      * Descends into subdirectories, because [scanOne] does. When the two
340:      * disagreed the screen said "14 games" and then listed none of them: the
341:      * count walked the whole tree while this only ever read the top level, so
342:      * a library organised one-folder-per-game - which is the normal way to
343:      * keep them - looked empty. Anything the counter counts must be listable,
344:      * or the count is a lie.
345:      *
346:      * Read at the moment of asking rather than served from the library cache,
347:      * so a file copied over USB a second ago is listed and one deleted a second
348:      * ago is not.
349:      */
350:     fun listGames(
351:         context: Context,
352:         uriString: String,
353:         maxDepth: Int = 1,
354:         stillWanted: () -> Boolean = { true }
355:     ): List<Entry> {
356:         val resolver = context.applicationContext.contentResolver
357:         val tree = runCatching { Uri.parse(uriString) }.getOrNull() ?: return emptyList()
358:         val root = childrenUriFor(tree) ?: return emptyList()
359:         val out = mutableListOf<Entry>()
360: 
361:         // Same walk, same guard and the same depth as the counter, so the two
362:         // cannot drift apart again.
363:         val queue = ArrayDeque<Triple<Uri, String, Int>>()
364:         queue.add(Triple(root, "", maxDepth))
365:         var guard = 0
366:         val seen = HashSet<String>()
367: 
368:         while (queue.isNotEmpty() && guard < MAX_DIRECTORIES) {
369:             guard++
370:             if (!stillWanted()) break
371:             // Верхняя граница на размер ответа.
372:             //
373:             // Список строился без ограничений, а каждая запись - это
374:             // три строки. На папке с несколькими тысячами файлов (обычное
375:             // дело для дампа) он занимал десятки мегабайт, и всё это
376:             // передавалось в адаптер разом. На 3 ГБ памяти это тот самый
377:             // вылет по нехватке памяти при открытии папки.
378:             if (out.size >= MAX_ENTRIES) break
379:             val (children, prefix, depth) = queue.removeFirst()
380:             val cursor = runCatching {
381:                 resolver.query(
382:                     children,
383:                     arrayOf(
384:                         DocumentsContract.Document.COLUMN_DOCUMENT_ID,
385:                         DocumentsContract.Document.COLUMN_DISPLAY_NAME,
386:                         DocumentsContract.Document.COLUMN_MIME_TYPE,
387:                         DocumentsContract.Document.COLUMN_SIZE
388:                     ),
389:                     null, null, null
390:                 )
391:             }.getOrNull() ?: continue
392: 
393:             runCatching {
394:             cursor.use {
395:                 while (it.moveToNext()) {
396:                     if (out.size >= MAX_ENTRIES) break
397:                     val documentId = it.getString(0)
398:                     val name = it.getString(1) ?: continue
399:                     val mime = it.getString(2) ?: ""
400:                     val size = if (it.isNull(3)) 0L else it.getLong(3)
401: 
402:                     if (mime == DocumentsContract.Document.MIME_TYPE_DIR) {
403:                         if (depth > 1 &&
404:                             documentId != null &&
405:                             seen.add(documentId) &&
406:                             !isLayoutName(name)
407:                         ) {
408:                             runCatching {
409:                                 queue.add(
410:                                     Triple(
411:                                         DocumentsContract.buildChildDocumentsUriUsingTree(tree, documentId),
412:                                         if (prefix.isEmpty()) name else "$prefix/$name",
413:                                         depth - 1
414:                                     )
415:                                 )
416:                             }
417:                         }
418:                         continue
419:                     }
420: 
421:                     if (isRom(name)) {
422:                         out.add(Entry(name, size, prefix))
423:                     }
424:                 }
425:             }
426:             }
427:         }
428:         return out.sortedByDescending { it.bytes }
429:     }
430: 
431:     private fun childrenUriFor(tree: Uri): Uri? = runCatching {
432:         DocumentsContract.buildChildDocumentsUriUsingTree(
433:             tree,
434:             DocumentsContract.getTreeDocumentId(tree)
435:         )
436:     }.getOrNull()
437: 
438:     /**
439:      * The document URI of a file this scanner listed.
440:      *
441:      * The scanner records a name and a sub-path rather than a URI, because a
442:      * URI is large and most callers only want to count. Rebuilding it here
443:      * keeps that trade without making the folder screen re-walk the tree.
444:      *
445:      * Document ids under a tree are the tree's own id plus the relative path,
446:      * which is how the storage framework addresses children; when a provider
447:      * does not follow that shape the caller gets null and says so rather than
448:      * launching something wrong.
449:      */
450:     fun childUri(treeUriString: String, entry: Entry): Uri? = runCatching {
451:         val tree = Uri.parse(treeUriString)
452:         val rootId = DocumentsContract.getTreeDocumentId(tree)
453:         val suffix = if (entry.relativePath.isEmpty()) entry.name
454:                      else entry.relativePath + "/" + entry.name
455:         val childId = if (rootId.endsWith("/")) rootId + suffix else "$rootId/$suffix"
456:         DocumentsContract.buildDocumentUriUsingTree(tree, childId)
457:     }.getOrNull()
458: 
459:     /** The part of the path a person would call the folder's name. */
460:     fun displayNameOf(uriString: String): String {
461:         val decoded = runCatching { Uri.decode(uriString) }.getOrDefault(uriString)
462:         val tail = decoded.substringAfterLast(':', decoded.substringAfterLast('/'))
463:         return tail.substringAfterLast('/').ifBlank { decoded }
464:     }
465: 
466:     /**
467:      * Total bytes under a plain filesystem directory.
468:      *
469:      * Keys, firmware, saves and the shader cache live in the data root as
470:      * ordinary files, not behind a document tree, so they are measured with
471:      * [java.io.File] rather than the content resolver. Returns 0 for a missing
472:      * directory, which is the honest answer for "nothing installed".
473:      */
474:     fun directoryBytes(path: String?): Long {
475:         if (path.isNullOrBlank()) return 0L
476:         val root = java.io.File(path)
477:         if (!root.exists()) return 0L
478:         if (root.isFile) return root.length()
479: 
480:         var total = 0L
481:         var guard = 0
482:         val queue = ArrayDeque<java.io.File>()
483:         queue.add(root)
484:         while (queue.isNotEmpty() && guard < MAX_DIRECTORIES) {
485:             guard++
486:             val entries = queue.removeFirst().listFiles() ?: continue
487:             for (entry in entries) {
488:                 if (entry.isDirectory) queue.add(entry) else total += entry.length()
489:             }
490:         }
491:         return total
492:     }
493: 
494:     /** Formats bytes the way a storage screen would. */
495:     fun humanSize(bytes: Long): String {
496:         if (bytes <= 0) return "0 MB"
497:         val gb = bytes / 1_073_741_824.0
498:         if (gb >= 1.0) return String.format(Locale.US, "%.1f GB", gb)
499:         val mb = bytes / 1_048_576.0
500:         if (mb >= 1.0) return String.format(Locale.US, "%.0f MB", mb)
501:         return String.format(Locale.US, "%.0f KB", bytes / 1024.0)
502:     }
503: 
504:     /** Stops a symlink loop or an absurd tree from hanging the scan. */
505:     private const val MAX_DIRECTORIES = 400
506: 
507:     /**
508:      * Потолок на длину списка файлов.
509:      *
510:      * Не про «столько игр не бывает», а про память: список целиком лежит
511:      * в куче и целиком уходит в адаптер. Три тысячи строк экран всё равно
512:      * не покажет осмысленно, а вылет по нехватке памяти покажет.
513:      */
514:     private const val MAX_ENTRIES = 3000
515: }

## v21 — the launcher showed one game and would not open the rest

**Reported:** «одну игру видит а остальные не видит а раз не видит то и не
открывает либо проблема в том что лаунчер не прокручивается влево вправо может
поэтому не видит».

The guess in the report — that the rail does not scroll — is the one thing that
was **not** wrong.

### Cause (mine)

`renderLauncher()` built the carousel out of `visibleGames()`, and that function
applies the search box and the filter chips of the **Список** tab:

```js
RAIL_LIST = visibleGames();   // поиск и FILTER — принадлежности «Списка»
```

Type anything into «Найти игру…», or leave a chip on «Сейв», and the carousel
shrank to whatever survived the filter. The other games were not off-screen —
they were not in the rail at all, so the dock's «Запустить» could not reach them
either.

Worse, `FILTER = 'fresh'` produced an **empty** rail and the message «нет игр —
откройте Список и добавьте папку» with a full library sitting behind it.

Scrolling was never broken: with 8 games the rail scrolls 623 px and ‹ › both
work. What made it *look* broken is the presentation — the scrollbar is hidden
(`scrollbar-width:none`) and only ~1.5 slides fit (`padding: 8px 18vw`, `.slide`
is `min(42vw, 220px)`), so a single tile on screen is the normal appearance of a
carousel holding many games.

### Fix

`railGames()` returns the whole library; the search box and the chips stay in
«Список», which is the tab they belong to. Both go through the same
`sortGames()`, so the two tabs cannot drift apart in order. The dock prints
`3 / 12`, so the size of the library is on screen and one tile can never again be
read as «одна игра».

### Proof

Measured in Chromium against the real page — one library of 8 games, six states:

```
                                  rail slides   list rows
search "номер 3" in Список              1            1    <- the report
filter Сейв (one game has a save)       1            1    <- the report
filter Не играли                        0            0    <- "нет игр" over 8 games
after the fix, every state              8            as filtered
```

`tests/LauncherRailTest.kt` models the logic and then checks the shipped page:
it fails on the old file (4 checks) and passes on the new one. It also asserts
that `docs/library.html` and `patch/android/assets/library.html` are
byte-identical — the APK is served the second one, so a fix applied to only the
first would never reach the phone.

**Files:** `docs/library.html`, `patch/android/assets/library.html`,
`tests/LauncherRailTest.kt`

Now let me look at library.html rail code in detail (lines ~200-260, 480-520, 760-900, 1470-1520) to see the current state and find remaining issues.

Also, the user says "чтобы видел игры все от приставки" — the games from the console. Hmm, "приставка" could also be a game console... but in the context of this project, "игры от приставки" = games dumped from the console. So the scan must find all of them.

Real bug candidates for "only one game visible":

The scan `addGamesRecursive` requires `GameMetadata.getIsValid(filePath)` → needs keys. Keys gate is present.

But there's a subtle one: `getGame(it.uri, true, false)` → `GameMetadata.getIsValid(filePath)` — after `GameMetadata.resetMetadata()`. Should be fine for multiple files.

Hmm — what about `mountedContainerUris`? no.

Consider a folder-per-game layout (`Games/GameTitle/game.nsp`) with deepScan=false: depth=1, so directories are not descended → 0 games. With deepScan=true: depth 3 → works. The user might not have deep scan on. But the user says they see ONE game. If they have one file at the top level plus subfolders, they'd see exactly one.

Another: `GameFormats.isLaunchable(filename)` where `FileUtil.getFilename(uri)` — in upstream yuzu Eden, `getFilename` returns the name **without** extension? Let me check: yuzu's `FileUtil.getFilename`:

```kotlin
fun getFilename(uri: Uri): String? {
    val name = queryName(uri)
    return name ?: uri.toString().substringAfterLast('/')
}
```
And `queryName` returns display name with extension. So fine.

But `GameFormats.isLaunchable(filename)` returns true for names "main" and "00" — needs full filename. Fine.

So the most probable single-game cause: depth 1 with a nested library. And the presentation issue: rail shows ~1.5 tiles.

But wait — there may be a genuine remaining bug. Let me look at library.html rail more carefully, particularly the horizontal scroll behavior, the `fillCover` drag issue, and the re-centering. And check the `LAUNCH_I` handling.

Let me read the relevant portions of docs/library.html.

Now I have a good picture of the launcher. Let me now check the WebView setup in LivePanelFragment.kt — is there a JS bridge `games()` etc., and importantly: does the WebView block the rail's horizontal scrolling? Also check `Spaces.kt` and `patch/android/assets/library.html` is identical (yes).

Now, the critical issue: "видит только одну игру". Given BUGS.md v21 claims railGames fix is already in, and the user still reports it — either they have an older APK, or there's a remaining root cause.

Let me think harder about what could produce exactly one game in GAMES.

`LivePanel.gamesJson()` → `rememberedGames()`:
- If keys absent → emptyList → zero games, and the UI shows the "Папка есть, но игр нет. Если ключи ✕" hint.
- else: `GameHelper.cachedGameList` if non-empty; else prefs KEY_GAMES.

`GameHelper.getGames()`:
- keys absent → wipes cache, returns empty.
- Otherwise scans.

Now here's a serious one I should verify: `GameMetadata.getIsValid(filePath)`. In upstream yuzu, GameMetadata caches by path, and `getIsValid` returns `GameInfo::Find(...)` valid. If a ROM's header can't be parsed (e.g., .nsp is a PFS0 image), it returns false → game skipped. Fine normally.

Hmm, what about the *cache* path: `preferences.getStringSet(KEY_GAMES, ...)`. **SharedPreferences `getStringSet` returns a set that must not be modified.** `stored.mapNotNull{...}` creates a new list — fine.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Builds and runs the host test suite against a patched Eden checkout.
#
# Two things here are easy to get wrong and both make the suite worthless:
#
#  1. Do NOT put <eden>/src/common on the include path. Eden ships its own
#     common/assert.h, which shadows the standard <cassert>; every assert()
#     then expands to nothing and the tests pass without checking anything.
#     Only -I<eden>/src is correct.
#
#  2. Eden's logging is a real dependency of the layer. Rather than linking
#     half the emulator, a tiny stub supplies FmtLogMessageImpl.
#
# Usage: bash tools/run_tests.sh [--eden <dir>]
set -uo pipefail

EDEN_DIR="${EDEN_DIR:-/tmp/citest}"
# A test that will not link proves nothing. Allow a known few (they need most
# of video_core), but fail if the number grows - that means the environment is
# broken, not the code.
MAX_SKIP="${MAX_SKIP:-99}"
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --max-skip) MAX_SKIP="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --eden) EDEN_DIR="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    *) echo "unknown argument: $1" >&2; exit 2 ;;
  esac
done

E="$EDEN_DIR"
S="$E/src/common/symbiosis"
[ -d "$S" ] || { echo "patched Eden not found at $E (run tools/apply_patch.sh first)" >&2; exit 1; }

HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"

# Eden's logging.h needs fmt 10 (format.get()); Ubuntu ships fmt 9. Point
# FMT_INCLUDE at a fmt 10 checkout to build against that instead. FMT_HEADER_ONLY
# avoids needing the compiled library at all.
FMT_FLAGS=""
if [ -n "${FMT_INCLUDE:-}" ]; then
  FMT_FLAGS="-isystem $FMT_INCLUDE -DFMT_HEADER_ONLY"
  LINK_FMT=""
else
  LINK_FMT="-lfmt"
fi
BUILD=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$BUILD"' EXIT

# Minimal stand-in for Eden's logging backend.
cat > "$BUILD/log_stub.cpp" <<'STUB'
#include <cstdarg>
#include <string_view>
#include "common/logging.h"
namespace Common::Log {
void FmtLogMessageImpl(Class, Level, const char*, unsigned int, const char*,
                       fmt::string_view, const fmt::format_args&) {}
} // namespace Common::Log
STUB

CORE="$S/symbiosis_log.cpp $S/symbiosis_types.cpp $BUILD/log_stub.cpp"
# Settings::values lives here; several tests read or write real settings.
SETTINGS="$E/src/common/settings.cpp"

deps_for() {
  case "$1" in
    t_mali|t_parse) echo "$S/mali_tuning.cpp $CORE" ;;
    t_fw)           echo "$S/firmware_vault.cpp $CORE" ;;
    t_rom)          echo "$S/rom_tools.cpp $CORE" ;;
    t_save)         echo "$S/save_guard.cpp $S/thermal_monitor.cpp $CORE" ;;
    t_guard)        echo "$CORE" ;;
    t_modes)        echo "$S/auto_modes.cpp $S/device_profiles.cpp $SETTINGS $CORE" ;;
    t_uaf)          echo "$S/memory_governor.cpp $CORE" ;;
    t_v12)          echo "$S/device_profiles.cpp $S/auto_modes.cpp $SETTINGS $CORE" ;;
    t_fps)          echo "$S/device_profiles.cpp $S/auto_modes.cpp $SETTINGS $CORE" ;;
    *)              echo "" ;;
  esac
}

pass=0; fail=0; skip=0; failed=""
for f in "$HERE"/tests/t_*.cpp; do
  [ -e "$f" ] || continue
  n=$(basename "$f" .cpp)
  # shellcheck disable=SC2046
  # shellcheck disable=SC2086
  if g++ -std=c++20 -O1 $FMT_FLAGS -I"$E/src" -o "$BUILD/$n" "$f" $(deps_for "$n") $LINK_FMT \
       > "$BUILD/$n.err" 2>&1; then
    if out=$("$BUILD/$n" 2>&1); then
      echo "  PASS  $n — $(printf '%s' "$out" | tail -1)"; pass=$((pass+1))
    else
      echo "  FAIL  $n"; printf '%s\n' "$out" | tail -5 | sed 's/^/        /'
      fail=$((fail+1)); failed="$failed $n"
    fi
  else
    # A test whose dependencies are not wired up is reported, never hidden.
    # A test that will not build is reported with the real reason, never a
    # blank. An empty parenthesis told me nothing on CI and cost a whole run.
    reason=$(grep -m1 -E "undefined reference|error:|fatal error:" "$BUILD/$n.err" | head -1)
    echo "  SKIP  $n"
    echo "        reason: ${reason:-unknown}"
    sed 's/^/        | /' "$BUILD/$n.err" | head -6
    skip=$((skip+1))
  fi
done

# Kotlin tests, when a compiler is available.
if command -v kotlinc >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  for f in "$HERE"/tests/*.kt; do
    [ -e "$f" ] || continue
    n=$(basename "$f" .kt)
    kotlinc "$f" -include-runtime -d "$BUILD/$n.jar" 2>/dev/null
    # Run from the repository root. A test that reads its own subject - as
    # PanelAssetsTest does, checking docs/ and the shell source against the
    # copy of the routing logic it asserts - resolves those paths relative to
    # the working directory, and CI invokes this script from elsewhere. The JS
    # loop below already does this; the Kotlin one did not, so the same test
    # passed locally and failed on the runner.
    if out=$(cd "$HERE" && java -jar "$BUILD/$n.jar" 2>&1); then
      echo "  PASS  $n — $(printf '%s' "$out" | tail -1)"; pass=$((pass+1))
    else
      echo "  FAIL  $n"; printf '%s\n' "$out" | tail -8 | sed 's/^/        /'
      fail=$((fail+1)); failed="$failed $n"
    fi
  done
else
  echo "  note: kotlinc not on PATH, Kotlin tests not run"
fi

# Node tests. The capability layer spawns real interpreters, so these check
# actual process behaviour rather than a mock; they need node on PATH and
# python3 for the Python-runtime cases.
if command -v node >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  for f in "$HERE"/tests/*.js; do
    [ -e "$f" ] || continue
    n=$(basename "$f" .js)
    if out=$(cd "$HERE" && node "$f" 2>&1); then
      echo "  PASS  $n — $(printf '%s' "$out" | tail -1)"; pass=$((pass+1))
    else
      echo "  FAIL  $n"; printf '%s\n' "$out" | tail -15 | sed 's/^/        /'
      fail=$((fail+1)); failed="$failed $n"
    fi
  done
else
  echo "  note: node not on PATH, JS tests not run"
fi

echo
echo "passed=$pass failed=$fail skipped=$skip"
[ "$fail" -eq 0 ] || { echo "failing:$failed"; exit 1; }
if [ "$skip" -gt "$MAX_SKIP" ]; then
  echo "too many tests could not be built ($skip > $MAX_SKIP): the toolchain is"
  echo "missing something - libfmt-dev, or the patched Eden tree."
  exit 1
fi

parts.text:
kotlinc, java, node are available. So I can run the Kotlin and JS tests (not the C++ ones without an Eden tree).

Now, decision time. What should I actually change?

The user's complaint: "почини чтобы видел игры все от приставки" — fix so it sees all games from the console. Plus horizontal navigation.

Root causes I'll fix:

**A. Scan depth — the big one.** A console dump (`/sdcard/Games/`) is typically organized as one folder per game, or the user picks `/sdcard` and games live deeper. With `deepScan=false` (default when adding a folder? need to check where GameDir is created), the library import walks depth 1 and misses every nested game. Fix: make the import depth match the counter AND make it deep enough to find games in subfolders. But changing the default of `deepScan` might be intrusive. Let me check where GameDir(deepScan) is created — GameFoldersFragment / pick. Let me look.

Actually a cleaner fix that respects upstream: in `GameHelper`, when a folder yields no launchable files at depth 1 but has subdirectories, retry at depth 3. Hmm, that's a "second pass" heuristic. But it's deterministic and cheap-ish (only when depth-1 found nothing).

But careful: the counter (`GameFolderScanner.scan`) must agree, else the count lies. The docstring already says the counter should match the importer. So the cleanest: introduce a single shared "effective depth" used by both the importer and the counter: `depthFor(dir)` = 3 when deepScan else 1... and the auto-retry must be reflected in both.

Simplest coherent design: one function in GameFolderScanner:
```kotlin
fun depthFor(deepScan: Boolean): Int = if (deepScan) 3 else 1
```
plus a new shared decision: the *library* depth is at least NESTED_FALLBACK_DEPTH when the top level holds no games. That requires reading disk twice, and both readers must do it identically to stay in sync. Risky for drift.

Alternative cleaner approach: make the depth itself adaptive in one place, used by both:

```kotlin
/** Глубина, на которой библиотека реально ищет игры. */
fun depthFor(dir: GameDir): Int = if (dir.deepScan) DEEP_SCAN_DEPTH else SHALLOW_SCAN_DEPTH
```
and have the *folder picker* default to deepScan = true. Hmm, but existing users' saved dirs have deepScan=false in config.

Better idea: since the failure mode is "games in subfolders are invisible", and the counter must not lie, do the adaptive rule in ONE function that both call, implemented as: if `deepScan` → 3, else 1 **but** the importer/counter both fall back to 3 when the shallow pass found zero games. The "zero games" condition is observable identically by both (they both walk the same tree with the same rules). So a shared helper:

```kotlin
fun scanDepths(deepScan: Boolean): List<Int> = if (deepScan) listOf(3) else listOf(1, 3)
```
Both the importer and the counter iterate the list of depths and use the first that yields games; the counter sums... no, the counter must count each file once. If shallow yields 0, use deep. Since shallow yielding 0 means the deep pass will be the only pass, there's no double counting. If shallow yields >0, use shallow only.

That's implementable: `scanOne(context, uri, depths)` — walk at max depth = depths.last(), and track whether any game was found at depth 1... Hmm, no: the walk is a single BFS; I can record for each found game its depth. Then apply the rule: if deepScan → include all found (depth ≤ 3). If !deepScan → include only games found at depth 1, unless none were found at depth 1, in which case include all found within depth 3.

That is a clean single-pass rule, identical in both readers, and it preserves the existing GameCountTest semantics for the "deepScan on" case. But GameCountTest asserts "depth 1 misses a nested game, as upstream does" — that's a *model* test of the counting function, and my change adds the fallback. I'd need to update that test to pin the new rule. That's legitimate — the test pins a behavior that is precisely the bug. But I must be careful: is changing this "correct" for the user's setup? The user says games from the console aren't all visible. If their dump is flat, depth 1 works. If nested, it doesn't. The fallback only kicks in when depth 1 finds zero games — it can only *add* games the user has, never remove. Safe.

Hmm, wait. But actually — what if depth 1 finds exactly ONE game (the user's report: "видит только одну игру") and the rest are nested? Then the fallback wouldn't trigger! That's the exact case. Ugh.

So the rule should be: for !deepScan, use depth 1 **plus** descend into subdirectories, but exclude layout dirs. I.e. essentially "always recurse" like the counter's docstring claims. The risk of always recursing: walking nand/load/cache — but `isLayoutName` prevents descending into those, and LAYOUT_NAMES covers the layout dirs. That's exactly why `isLayoutName` exists. And GameHelper's `addGamesRecursive` has no layout guard at all — a real gap: if the data root is a game dir, it walks nand (hundreds of NCAs).

So the correct fix: the importer should recurse like the counter does, honouring `isLayoutName` and the depth ceiling. And when deepScan is on, ceiling 3; when off... if we always recurse, the ceiling is what matters. Let me settle:

- `GameFolderScanner.depthFor(deepScan)` stays as the ceiling: 3 / 1. Hmm, but then a folder-per-game library still breaks with deepScan off.

Decision: raise the shallow ceiling to 3 as well, i.e. `depthFor` returns 3 always? Then `deepScan` becomes meaningless. Actually why not: make the library always look 3 levels deep, with layout names never descended. That is exactly "always descends into subdirectories... the deep_scan flag governs what the emulator's own library importer does" — we change the importer to match the counter's *documented* behaviour, and keep the 3-level ceiling as the guard against a pathological tree. The `deepScan` flag then only remains for... nothing. But we can't remove the field (upstream model + config). We can keep honoring it as "at least this depth" and treat the flag as obsolete-by-design with a comment.

Wait — careful about drift with the counter: `scanOne` is called with `depthFor(dir.deepScan)`. If I change `depthFor` to a constant 3, both importer and counter use 3 automatically. One function, both callers. Minimal, provable, and no double-count risk. Tests: GameCountTest pins `count(nested, LAUNCHABLE, 1).first == 0` — that's a model of a generic function with a maxDepth param, not of `depthFor`. I can add checks pinning `depthFor(false) == 3` and the layout-name skip. GameCountTest's own checks remain valid as a statement about the generic walker... but the check name says "as upstream does" which will now be wrong. I'll update the names/assertions to reflect the new rule: at depth 3 a nested game is found; and the layout dir is never descended.

Hmm, but hold on. Is depth 3 enough for a console dump? Common layouts:
- `/sdcard/Games/*.nsp` → depth 1 ✓
- `/sdcard/Games/GameName/game.nsp` → depth 2 ✓
- `/sdcard/Switch/Game [0100XXXXXXXXX]/game.nsp` → depth 3 ✓
- `/sdcard/Games/GameName/Exefs/main` → depth 3 ✓

Deeper (4+) is unusual. But the 400-directory guard bounds it. I could make it generous: walk the whole tree with the existing MAX_DIRECTORIES=400 guard and layout skip, with no depth ceiling. That eliminates the "my games are 4 levels down" class of bug permanently, and the 400 guard is the real protection. Risk: performance on a huge tree — but 400 SAF queries max, plus layout skip. That's acceptable and matches the counter's existing MAX_DIRECTORIES guard.

Hmm, but the *importer* parses every ROM header (expensive). Walking 400 dirs of random junk with few games is fine. Parsing is per-game, not per-dir.

I'll go with: single `GameFolderScanner.scanDepthFor()` = MAX depth = no ceiling (i.e. effectively `Int.MAX_VALUE`) — but I want a named constant to keep both readers in sync, and the tests can pin it. Let me define:

```kotlin
/**
 * Насколько глубоко библиотека ищет игры.
 *
 * Раньше здесь стояло 3 при глубоком скане и 1 без него, и рельс/счётчик
 * брали это же число. Итог был один: дамп с приставки, где на каждую
 * игру своя папка, приносил ровно одну игру - ту, что лежала в корне.
 * Теперь обход не ограничен по глубине; его ограничивают каталоги
 * раскладки (nand/load/cache/...) и потолок в 400 каталогов.
 */
const val SCAN_DEPTH = 8   // hmm
```

A concrete number is better than Int.MAX_VALUE for testability and reviewability. But any fixed number can hide a game. With MAX_DIRECTORIES=400 as the real guard, depth 8 is generous and bounded. Hmm, but "8" is arbitrary and the user could have 9. Honestly the guard is directories, not depth. I'll use `Int.MAX_VALUE`? A test pinning `depthFor(false) == Int.MAX_VALUE` looks odd but is honest: no depth ceiling.

Let me reconsider: simplest honest API:

```kotlin
fun depthFor(@Suppress("UNUSED_PARAMETER") deepScan: Boolean): Int = MAX_DEPTH  // где MAX_DEPTH = 8?
```

Hmm. I keep going in circles. Let me look at what the actual risk is: recursion in `addGamesRecursive` is recursive Kotlin (stack) — deep trees could overflow. `scanOne`/`listGames` are iterative BFS with the 400 guard. For the importer, converting `addGamesRecursive` to a bounded BFS with a directory budget matching the counter is the right move, and then depth ceiling = the directory budget. That kills two birds: no stack risk, bounded work, and a shared constant.

Plan for GameHelper:
- Replace `addGamesRecursive` recursion with the same iterative BFS shape used by `GameFolderScanner`, with a shared budget constant and `isLayoutName` skip.
- Depth: no artificial ceiling beyond the budget; but keep a `MAX_DEPTH` constant equal to the guard so both readers share it.

Actually — better factoring: put the *shared* rules in GameFolderScanner (which both already depend on):
- `const val MAX_SCAN_DEPTH` / `fun depthFor(deepScan)` 
- `isLayoutName` (exists)
- `MAX_DIRECTORIES` → make it internal/public so the importer uses the same budget. Currently `private const val MAX_DIRECTORIES = 400`. I'll expose `const val MAX_DIRECTORIES` (public) — or add `const val BUDGET_DIRECTORIES`. Simpler: make it public and use it in GameHelper.

Now **B. Keys gate wiping the library.** `GameHelper.getGames()` returns emptyList and clears `cachedGameList` when keys are absent, and `LivePanel.rememberedGames()` returns emptyList when keys are absent. Combined: no keys ⇒ the launcher shows zero games, even though a previous successful scan cached them with real titles. The user then thinks "приложение не видит игры". And since startup never rescans, it stays blank. Fix: don't blank the cache; keep serving remembered games (titles/paths) so the list is at least visible, and keep the status strip's "keys ✕" as the honest signal. I'll change:
- `GameHelper`: on `!keysOk`, do not clear `cachedGameList`; return the persisted cache instead of emptyList? Careful: `getGames()` result is written to prefs only at the end; the early return skips the write, so prefs survives. Returning remembered games from `getGames()` would keep the UI stable. But it also means "scan" reports stale games as if fresh. Hmm. The comment says: "Не кладём такие записи и не затираем прошлый кэш пустотой" (don't put such records and don't overwrite the past cache with emptiness) — but the code DOES wipe `cachedGameList`. So the code contradicts its own stated intent. Fix: don't clear `cachedGameList`, and return the remembered list (from prefs) so the screen keeps what it had. That matches the comment and fixes the "keys missing ⇒ zero games" report.

Hmm, but is that right? Without keys, the game titles come from the cache; the games still *launch* (restoreContentForGame reloads keys; if keys are missing they won't decrypt, so launching fails). Showing them is more honest than hiding them: the status strip says keys ✕. And the WebView already shows "Если ключи ✕ — сначала ключи, не сканер." in the empty state. So: if there are remembered games, show them. Yes.

**C. `rememberedGames()` gate on keys** — same fix: drop the `if (!keysPresent()) return emptyList()` so a cached library is shown even without keys (the JSON already carries `keys`).

Careful: `SetupStatus.games()` reads `rememberedGames()` for the status strip, documented as "must not walk disk" — fine, cache only.

**D. GamesFragment: empty emission never clears the list** (`:229-233`). Let me read GamesFragment around there to fix properly. Symptom: after a rescan that finds nothing, the old list stays. Also: after a rescan that finds 1, list = 1 — no guard. Let me look.

**E. The rail.** Fixes:
1. `renderLauncher()` rebuilds `rail.innerHTML` and re-centers on every `loadGames()`, which the 700 ms `findGames()` poll calls up to 20 times → the rail jumps back to tile 0 mid-swipe. Fix: only rebuild when the identity of the list changed; keep `LAUNCH_I` by game path across rebuilds.
2. Image drag steals horizontal swipe: add `draggable="false"`, CSS `user-select:none; -webkit-user-drag:none; -webkit-touch-callout:none` on `.slide img`/`.slide`.
3. `scrollIntoView` scrolls all ancestors → replace with `rail.scrollTo({left: ...})` computed from `offsetLeft - (clientWidth - offsetWidth)/2`. Safer, and it can't drag the page.
4. `nearestSlide()` should ignore while a programmatic smooth scroll is in flight? Simpler: it already debounces. But with snap + smooth scrolling, a tap on ‹ triggers smooth scroll and the scroll listener may set a different index. Use a `PROGRAMMATIC` flag with a timestamp to ignore scroll events for ~350 ms after snapTo.
5. Keyboard/arrow support: add `keydown` for ArrowLeft/ArrowRight on the document when the launch tab is on → step LAUNCH_I. Useful for a "влево-вправо" expectation (the user may be using a gamepad/D-pad! "влево-вправо" could be the D-pad on a controller... but the launcher is a WebView; a connected gamepad D-pad wouldn't scroll). Hmm — if the user means a physical D-pad, we'd need Gamepad API handling. That's a stretch. But cheap: add arrow-key handling.
6. Make it obviously scrollable: the hidden scrollbar + 1.5 visible tiles. Could add a visible hint. The `.pos` counter already exists. Maybe reduce side padding so ~2.5 tiles show. `padding: 8px 18vw` — that's the padding that makes only ~1.5 tiles visible. I'll leave the aesthetics mostly alone but add a subtle "edge" gradient + a `touch-action: pan-x`/`overscroll-behavior-x: contain` to stop the WebView's parent from stealing. Hmm, `overscroll-behavior` matters: without it, a horizontal overscroll at the end of the rail can bubble to the WebView page. Add `overscroll-behavior-x:contain`.
7. Also `touch-action: pan-x` on the rail so vertical page scroll still works but horizontal is owned by the rail.

Also: the space/tab switching — `body.space-kenji` hides the launch view. Not relevant.

**F. `‹ ›` buttons** — check they exist in HTML (line 402/404 per the report). Let me verify.

Now, how much should I do? The user asked to fix it. I should do a focused, well-tested change:

1. `GameFolderScanner`: shared, non-1-depth scan ceiling + public budget constant. 
2. `GameHelper`: iterative bounded walk with layout skip, shared depth; don't wipe cache when keys are missing.
3. `LivePanel.rememberedGames()`: don't blank on missing keys.
4. `GamesFragment`: clear the adapter on an empty emission.
5. `library.html` (+ assets copy): rail robustness — drag suppression, `rail.scrollTo`, keep selection across rebuilds, ignore scroll during programmatic snap, arrow keys.
6. Tests: extend `tests/LauncherRailTest.kt`? Better: add a new test file `tests/RailScrollTest.kt`? The repo convention is one test file per bug, with a header comment citing the report. I'll add `tests/DeepLibraryTest.kt` (models the walk: nested dump found at any depth, layout dirs skipped, budget respected) and extend `LauncherRailTest.kt` with the new rail checks (byte-identity already asserted there; the new page checks fit naturally there).
7. `docs/BUGS.md`: add a v22 entry in the established style.

Let me first verify a few things: the ‹ › buttons, the rail markup, whether `deepScan` is set true anywhere by default, and the GamesFragment code. Let me read library.html lines 380-420 and GamesFragment 200-260.

So a game folder added via the panel goes through `AddGameFolderDialogFragment` (upstream), which has a "deep scan" switch. Upstream's dialog: `AddGameFolderDialogFragment` has a switch "Recursive search" bound to `GameDir(uri, isDeepScan)`; the default in upstream is... In yuzu, `AddGameFolderDialogFragment` uses `view.findViewById<SwitchCompat>(R.id.recursive_search)` and default is unchecked? Let me recall: in yuzu's `AddGameFolderDialogFragment`, there's a `SwitchCompat` bound to `switchDeepScan`, and `buildGameDir` uses `switch.isChecked`. Default XML state unchecked → deepScan=false.

So by default, depth 1. If the user's console dump has subfolders → only top-level files appear. That is the single most probable root cause of "видит только одну игру": one .nsp at the root of the chosen folder, everything else inside per-game folders.

So my fix: the library must not be limited to depth 1. Design decision (final):

- `GameFolderScanner.depthFor(deepScan)`: keep the signature, but return the *maximum* depth allowed, which is now `SCAN_MAX_DEPTH` regardless — no. Hmm. If I make it a constant, the `deepScan` param becomes unused → the upstream dialog's switch becomes a lie.

Alternative that keeps the flag meaningful and fixes the bug: `depthFor(false) = 3` (was 1). Then the switch only matters for trees deeper than 3. That is a smaller, more honest change: "the shallow scan now means three levels, because a dump with a folder per game is the normal case." And GameFolderScanner's `MAX_DIRECTORIES` guard already bounds the work. Games deeper than 3 levels still need the switch — and the counter/importer agree either way, so the count never lies.

That's minimal, provable, and testable. I like it much better than a constant.

So: `fun depthFor(deepScan: Boolean): Int = if (deepScan) DEEP_SCAN_DEPTH else SHALLOW_SCAN_DEPTH` with `SHALLOW_SCAN_DEPTH = 3`, `DEEP_SCAN_DEPTH = 5`? Hmm — then deepScan must be > shallow. Let me set: shallow 3, deep 6. Both bounded; MAX_DIRECTORIES still the real guard.

And `GameHelper` line 110 must use `GameFolderScanner.depthFor(gameDir.deepScan)` instead of its own `if (gameDir.deepScan) 3 else 1` — the duplication is itself a bug source (that's how they drifted). Also add `isLayoutName` skip in the importer walk so raising the depth doesn't send it into nand/load/cache.

Also, `addGamesRecursive` is recursive; raising depth from 1 to 3 is fine (stack depth ≤6), no need to rewrite. But I'll add the layout guard and the directory budget to be safe? Recursive with depth ≤ 6 is bounded. Keep it simple: add layout skip + shared depthFor. Good.

Now the second half: **the rail**. And **the keys gate**. And **GamesFragment empty list**.

Let me also double check `FileUtil.listFiles` and `FileUtil.getExtension` semantics from upstream yuzu:
- `listFiles(treeUri: Uri): Array<MinimalDocumentFile>` — returns direct children.
- `getExtension(uri: Uri): String` — the extension WITHOUT the dot? In yuzu: 
```kotlin
fun getExtension(uri: Uri): String? = DocumentFile.fromSingleUri(...).name?.substringAfterLast(".", "")
```
Yes, no dot. And `Game.extensions` contains "xci" etc. without dot. Good.

`GameFormats.isLaunchable(filename)` where filename = `FileUtil.getFilename(uri)` — yuzu's getFilename returns the display name WITH extension. So `isLaunchable` works. But careful: in `addGamesRecursive`, `FileUtil.getFilename(it.uri)` — if it returns null, `isLaunchable(null)` would NPE. Upstream `getFilename` returns `String?`... In GameHelper:216 `GameFormats.isLaunchable(filename)` — if filename were nullable, Kotlin wouldn't compile against `String`. Since it compiles in their build (they claim builds pass), `getFilename` must return non-null `String`. Actually yuzu's signature: `fun getFilename(uri: Uri): String?`. Hmm, then `GameFormats.isLaunchable(filename)` with a `String?` wouldn't compile... unless Eden's version returns String. Let me not worry — the repo builds in CI.

Wait, actually this matters: if `getFilename` returns `String?` then this line wouldn't compile. Since CI builds the APK successfully, it must be non-null. OK.

Now let me also consider: **does the user maybe use the native GamesFragment (Список) rather than the WebView?** home_navigation startDestination is livePanelFragment, so the WebView is the home. The "Лаунчер" tab is the rail. So the rail fixes are the right target.

One more potential cause for "only one game": `LivePanel.gamesJson()` iterates `rememberedGames()`. And `LivePanelFragment.games()` at :254 — let me check whether it does something odd like only returning the first. Let me read that part of the bridge.

11: /**
12:  * Counts games and bytes per configured folder.
13:  *
14:  * Reads the tree directly through the content resolver instead of going via
15:  * [GameHelper], which parses every ROM header to build library metadata. That
16:  * is far too expensive for a screen whose only job is to say "14 games, 22 GB",
17:  * and it needs the encryption keys loaded; counting files needs neither.
18:  */
19: object GameFolderScanner {
20: 
21:     /**
22:      * Extensions the library will actually import.
23:      *
24:      * Same set as [GameFormats] / loader.cpp. GameHelper imports by this
25:      * list, not only Game.extensions, so XCI/NCA/NSO/KIP and a file named
26:      * "main" actually appear in the library.
27:      */
28:     private val ROM_EXTENSIONS = GameFormats.LAUNCHABLE
29: 
30:     /**
31:      * Всё, что человек считает файлом игры - включая то, что сам эмулятор
32:      * не откроет.
33:      *

36:      * пользователь про них знает. Панель "Мои игры" показывает их честно,
37:      * помечая как незапускаемые, вместо того чтобы делать вид, что папка
38:      * пуста - именно эта пустота и выглядит как "эмулятор ничего не нашёл".
39:      */

41: 
42:     /** Файл этого типа эмулятор запустить не сможет. */
43:     fun isLaunchable(name: String): Boolean = GameFormats.isLaunchable(name)
44: 
45:     /**
46:      * Плоский список файлов игр ровно в этой папке, без захода вглубь.
47:      *
48:      * Отдельно от [listGames], потому что вопросы разные: тот отвечает
49:      * "что импортирует библиотека", а этот - "что лежит в папке". Без
50:      * рекурсии, без фильтра по тому, примет ли файл эмулятор, и без
51:      * ограничения по количеству.
52:      */
53:     fun listFilesFlat(context: Context, uriString: String): List<Entry> {
54:         val resolver = context.applicationContext.contentResolver
55:         val tree = runCatching { Uri.parse(uriString) }.getOrNull() ?: return emptyList()
56:         val children = childrenUriFor(tree) ?: return emptyList()
57:         val out = mutableListOf<Entry>()
58:         val cursor = runCatching {
59:             resolver.query(
60:                 children,
61:                 arrayOf(
62:                     DocumentsContract.Document.COLUMN_DISPLAY_NAME,
63:                     DocumentsContract.Document.COLUMN_MIME_TYPE,
64:                     DocumentsContract.Document.COLUMN_SIZE
65:                 ),
66:                 null, null, null
67:             )
68:         }.getOrNull() ?: return emptyList()
69: 
70:         runCatching {
71:             cursor.use {
72:                 while (it.moveToNext()) {
73:                     if (out.size >= MAX_ENTRIES) break
74:                     val name = it.getString(0) ?: continue
75:                     val mime = it.getString(1) ?: ""
76:                     val size = if (it.isNull(2)) 0L else it.getLong(2)
77:                     if (mime == DocumentsContract.Document.MIME_TYPE_DIR) continue
